skill.name: mcp-builder
skill.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers in Python or TypeScript.
skill.summary: Build reliable MCP servers with clear tools, validation, documentation, and evaluations.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder credentials, documentation URLs, and template literals. The real security considerations are the evaluator running user-selected local commands and sending evaluation content to Anthropic.

remediation.issue: Evaluation harness can launch user-specified stdio commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run only trusted MCP servers and review commands before execution.

remediation.issue: Evaluation data is sent to Anthropic during scoring.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy notice and warn users not to evaluate confidential production data without approval.

remediation.issue: Credential examples use inline placeholder tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer redacted placeholders and remind users never to commit real API keys.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Harness Executes User-Supplied Commands
semantic_findings.description: The evaluator accepts a stdio command and arguments from the user, then passes them to the MCP stdio client. This is expected for local MCP testing, but it can execute arbitrary local programs when misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: CLI command and argument values flow into StdioServerParameters. The behavior is intentional and user-driven, but the local execution capability is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Data Sent to External LLM API
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation harness sends task questions, tool results, and conversation state to Anthropic Messages API. This is expected for scoring, but users could expose sensitive MCP data if they evaluate production systems.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly calls client.messages.create with the evaluation messages and tool definitions. The finding is about data exposure risk, not hidden malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Creating reliable MCP servers requires clear tool design, validation, and testing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through implementation patterns and evaluation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Plans MCP server scope, transport, tool names, and API coverage.
Guides TypeScript MCP SDK project structure and tool registration.
Guides Python FastMCP patterns with Pydantic validation.
Explains response formats, pagination, annotations, and error handling.
Creates XML evaluation tasks and describes how to run the evaluator.
Provides quality checklists for implementation and testing reviews.
limitations: It does not replace service-specific API documentation or credentials.
Reference examples use placeholder services and require adaptation.
Evaluation scripts require an Anthropic API key and a trusted MCP server.
SDK details can change, so current official documentation should be checked.

use_cases.title: Plan a new MCP integration
use_cases.description: Map a service API into focused tools with clear schemas, transport choices, and validation rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize server implementation
use_cases.description: Apply shared TypeScript or Python patterns for naming, pagination, errors, and response formatting.

use_cases.title: Create evaluation coverage
use_cases.description: Write realistic read-only questions and run them against an MCP server to measure tool usefulness.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple MCP Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a read-only MCP server for this service: [service]. Include tool names, required inputs, authentication, and response formats.

prompt_templates.title: Design TypeScript Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Design TypeScript MCP tools for these endpoints: [endpoints]. Include Zod inputs, annotations, pagination, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Python FastMCP Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Python FastMCP server for schema quality, tool descriptions, async API calls, response formatting, and security concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evaluation Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Create ten independent read-only evaluation questions for this MCP server. Include stable expected answers and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a GitHub issue search MCP server.
output_examples.output: A practical server plan with tool names, input fields, pagination, authentication, and evaluation ideas.

output_examples.input: Review my TypeScript MCP tool design.
output_examples.output: Focused feedback on naming, Zod schemas, annotations, response formats, and actionable error messages.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation questions for a project management MCP server.
output_examples.output: Ten read-only questions with stable answers, verification notes, and guidance for removing destructive tasks.

best_practices: Use explicit input schemas, limits, and annotations for every tool.
Keep tool outputs concise, paginated, and available in structured and readable formats.
Run evaluations with trusted servers and avoid sensitive production data.
anti_patterns: Do not expose broad tools that hide many unrelated operations behind one name.
Do not copy placeholder credentials or example URLs into production code.
Do not run evaluation commands for untrusted servers without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design, implement, document, and evaluate MCP servers for external services.

faq.question: Does it support both Python and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Python FastMCP and the TypeScript MCP SDK.

faq.question: Can it create evaluation tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains XML evaluation tasks and includes a harness for running them.

faq.question: Does it include production credentials?
faq.answer: No. Credential strings are placeholders. Users must provide their own secrets securely.

faq.question: Is network access required?
faq.answer: Some workflows fetch official documentation or call external service APIs during development and testing.

faq.question: What should users review before running scripts?
faq.answer: Review the target MCP server command, environment variables, remote URL, and data sent to the evaluator.
